findings.highlight: Supreme and all-knowing
findings.evidenceJa: 至高にして全なるもの
findings.governingReading: Their God is supreme and whole or all-encompassing.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes omniscience for totality.

findings.highlight: A spirit that created the perfect world.
findings.evidenceJa: 完璧な世界を作り上げた聖霊だ
findings.governingReading: The passage calls God the Holy Spirit that fashioned a perfect world.
findings.explanation: The English lowercases and genericizes the Holy Spirit as merely “a spirit.”

findings.highlight: Such a god would never allow evil to disgrace the world that he created.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの子である人を穢し、自らが創造した世界を汚す魔などを容認する道理がない
findings.governingReading: There is no reason God would tolerate demons that defile humans, his own children, and pollute the world he created.
findings.explanation: The English omits humans as God’s children and the distinct corruption of humanity.

findings.highlight: a necessary part of the world. It is something worthy of love
findings.evidenceJa: 主が構築した世界に必要な欠片、愛すべき被造物
findings.governingReading: Even threatening demons are necessary pieces of the Lord’s constructed world and created beings worthy of love.
findings.explanation: The English omits their explicit status as created beings and loosens the Lord’s authorship.

findings.highlight: producing gruesome tragedies
findings.evidenceJa: 凄惨な悲劇喜劇を演出する
findings.governingReading: Demons stage gruesome tragedies and comedies beyond human understanding.
findings.explanation: The English deletes “comedies,” removing the grotesque paired formulation.

findings.highlight: made people realize how powerless God is
findings.evidenceJa: 人の子に天の無力さを錯覚させた
findings.governingReading: Heaven’s designs sometimes caused humanity to mistake Heaven for powerless.
findings.explanation: The English promotes an explicitly false impression into realized fact and changes Heaven into God.

findings.highlight: a Command Spell
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪が数個
findings.governingReading: Kirei retains several still-powered Command Spells unused since the previous war.
findings.explanation: The English reduces several Command Spells to one.

findings.highlight: the selected Agents
findings.evidenceJa: 選ばれた代行者
findings.governingReading: The comparison invokes the Scripture-class armament said to be held by chosen Executors.
findings.explanation: The English switches established terminology from “Executors” to the generic “Agents.”

findings.highlight: You could have used the boy as bait to escape
findings.evidenceJa: 以前のおぬしならば小僧を撒き餌にしても逃げ切ろう
findings.governingReading: Zouken says the Kirei of old would have escaped even if it meant using Shirou as bait.
findings.explanation: The English removes the comparison with Kirei’s former character and makes it a mere available tactic.

findings.highlight: I know we will both die eventually
findings.evidenceJa: じき殺されるのは判っている
findings.governingReading: Kirei knows that he and Shirou will shortly be killed.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the imminence and the external killer.

findings.highlight: I can do nothing, even if I defeat Assassin here and move to help the boy
findings.evidenceJa: 助けに行ったところで間に合わん
findings.governingReading: Even if Kirei defeats Assassin and goes to help, he will not arrive in time.
findings.explanation: The English changes lateness into unspecified inability to do anything.

findings.highlight: I shall see through the battle of the Church’s outlier
findings.evidenceJa: 何処まで戦うか見届けて進ぜようぞ
findings.governingReading: Zouken grandly offers to watch how far the Church outlier can fight.
findings.explanation: The English omits the question of Kirei’s limit and produces the unnatural phrase “see through the battle.”

findings.highlight: my heart and muscles are about to stop
findings.evidenceJa: 心筋が硬直し停止しようとしている
findings.governingReading: His cardiac muscle is stiffening and trying to stop.
findings.explanation: The English splits one anatomical subject into his heart and all his muscles.

findings.highlight: My mind reacts to her frantic warning before my body does
findings.evidenceJa: 心より速く体が反応した
findings.governingReading: His body reacts to Illya’s whole-hearted warning faster than his conscious mind or heart.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the order, making mind react before body.

findings.highlight: the sword I had on my waist
findings.evidenceJa: 腰に下げていた黒鍵
findings.governingReading: Shirou readies the Black Key hanging at his waist.
findings.explanation: The English discards the established weapon name.

findings.highlight: I resist the impact with all my strength
findings.evidenceJa: 両手で、満身の力でその一撃に抵抗した
findings.governingReading: Shirou resists the single blow with both hands and all his strength.
findings.explanation: The English omits the two-handed physical stance.

findings.highlight: was deflected like nothing
findings.evidenceJa: 一方的に粉砕された
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s utmost resistance is one-sidedly pulverized.
findings.explanation: The English changes destruction into casual deflection.

findings.highlight: I accept my fate, but
findings.evidenceJa: 受け入れそうになった時
findings.governingReading: Shirou is on the verge of accepting unavoidable death when seeing Illya interrupts him.
findings.explanation: The English says he accepts it, erasing the incomplete threshold that Illya prevents him from crossing.

findings.highlight: it feels like I’ll explode if I take another
findings.evidenceJa: その一息だけで体がパン、と風船みたいに破裂しそう
findings.governingReading: Although starved for oxygen, even that one possible breath makes his body feel ready to pop like a balloon.
findings.explanation: The English invents a second breath and makes it the condition of explosion, reversing the paradox.

findings.highlight: I use all of my Magic Circuit
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路を総動員し
findings.governingReading: Shirou mobilizes all of his magical circuits.
findings.explanation: The English uses an ungrammatical singular “all of my Magic Circuit.”

findings.highlight: His body is covered by the black mud
findings.evidenceJa: 全身は黒い泥に侵食され
findings.governingReading: Berserker’s whole body is being eroded or invaded by black mud.
findings.explanation: The English turns active corruption into surface covering.

findings.highlight: He raises his axe-sword
findings.evidenceJa: 咆哮と共に
findings.governingReading: Berserker raises the axe-sword with a roar.
findings.explanation: The English omits the roar accompanying the action.

findings.highlight: The priest is about to end his life.
findings.evidenceJa: 神父は最期の時を迎えた
findings.governingReading: The narration presents the priest as having reached his final moment.
findings.explanation: “End his life” suggests deliberate suicide rather than apparent imminent death at an enemy’s hands.

findings.highlight: He will drive them into a corner by cutting their limbs and tiring their bodies.
findings.evidenceJa: 心臓を破裂寸前まで追い込んでいく
findings.governingReading: Assassin drives the body as far as the brink of cardiac rupture.
findings.explanation: The English omits the culminating physiological pressure entirely.

findings.highlight: The priest has blocked them and reached this ruin.
findings.evidenceJa: それを凌ぎながら森を抜け、この廃墟に辿り着いた
findings.governingReading: While surviving every lethal throw, Kirei passed through the forest and reached the ruin.
findings.explanation: The English omits his traversal out of the forest.

findings.highlight: The seven he threw were all dodged.
findings.evidenceJa: 弾丸の如く放った七本の黒鍵は、悉くがアサシンに躱され、何処かに消えていった
findings.governingReading: All seven Black Keys fired like bullets were evaded and vanished somewhere beyond the fight.
findings.explanation: The English omits their bullet-like speed and disappearance, both of which explain why only three remain.

findings.highlight: the temple, pancreas, and diaphragm
findings.evidenceJa: 眉間膵臓横隔膜
findings.governingReading: The three simultaneous targets are the point between the eyebrows, the pancreas, and the diaphragm.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the first target to the temple.

findings.highlight: the lightning flashes
findings.evidenceJa: まったく同時、一息で放たれた紫電
findings.governingReading: Three purple-lightning throws are released in one breath at exactly the same instant.
findings.explanation: The English omits their simultaneity, single-breath execution, and purple color.

findings.highlight: The Black Keys will certainly hit him.
findings.evidenceJa: この体勢で放てば黒鍵は命中する
findings.governingReading: The Black Keys will hit if released from this posture.
findings.explanation: The English removes the condition supplied by Kirei’s particular position.

findings.highlight: The inhuman action is like a cannon firing.
findings.evidenceJa: 冗談じみた上昇は、砲台の弾丸そのものだった
findings.governingReading: The absurd ascent is the very image of a cannon projectile.
findings.explanation: The English changes comic impossibility into inhumanity and compares the action to firing rather than Kirei to the projectile.

findings.highlight: Matou Zouken, the one who has been observing the battle
findings.evidenceJa: 神父の処刑を愉しんでいた間桐臓硯
findings.governingReading: Zouken has been enjoying what he believes is the priest’s execution.
findings.explanation: The English turns sadistic enjoyment and presumed execution into neutral observation.

findings.highlight: Ask for forgiveness here.
findings.evidenceJa: 許しはここに
findings.governingReading: Forgiveness is here.
findings.explanation: The English turns a declaration of present forgiveness into an imperative to request it.

findings.highlight: Kyrie eleison.
findings.evidenceJa: この魂に憐れみを
findings.governingReading: The displayed plea asks for mercy upon this soul while the ruby supplies the liturgical Kyrie eleison.
findings.explanation: The English retains only the liturgical phrase and loses the soul-specific written meaning.

findings.highlight: the systematic basis of their magic
findings.evidenceJa: 世界に固定化された魔術基盤
findings.governingReading: The Church’s teaching is a magical foundation fixed into the world, described as among the greatest anti-spirit magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English turns an ontologically world-fixed magical foundation into the vague “systematic basis of their magic.”

findings.highlight: the greatest weapon against spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 最大の対霊魔術
findings.governingReading: It is regarded as the highest or greatest class of anti-spirit magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English changes a technical classification of magecraft into a generic weapon.

findings.highlight: wandering souls
findings.evidenceJa: 肉の身より離れ、腐り狂いながらも世に迷う魂
findings.governingReading: The rite concerns a soul separated from flesh that wanders the world while rotting and maddened.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the separation from flesh and the soul’s corruption and madness.
